questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white backgrounds and black lettering. These signs tell you the rules of the road. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: To reduce your chance of having an accident, you should:

options.text: Try to blend into traffic and not be noticed by other drivers.
Not use turn signals unless you are traveling at night.
Use your turn signals when changing lanes and making turns.
Ride closely to the vehicle ahead of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signals when changing lanes and making turns.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, make sure other drivers can see you. Tell other drivers what you plan to do by using turn signals and your brake light. Stay at a safe distance from other vehicles. Look ahead 12 seconds and be ready for hazards.

questions.question: Riding at night is usually:

options.text: Easier than riding during the day because you can more easily see the lights of other vehicles.
More difficult than riding during the day because it is harder to see.
Less distracting than riding during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: More difficult than riding during the day because it is harder to see.
questions.explanation: Night riding is harder because you cannot see as well. It is also harder for other drivers to see you. Without natural light and shadows, it is harder to judge how far away things are.

questions.question: Which color should you wear to be seen?
questions.correctAnswerText: Orange
questions.explanation: Wear orange, red, yellow, or green clothing to be more visible. Wear bright colors at all times, day or night.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should:

options.text: Assume the passenger has traveled by motorcycle before.
Not assume the passenger has traveled by motorcycle before and explain the process.
Not bother with explaining anything since they are only a passenger and not in control of the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not assume the passenger has traveled by motorcycle before and explain the process.
questions.explanation: Your passenger needs to know how to ride safely. Do not assume they know what to do. Give your passenger clear instructions before every ride.

questions.question: The single most important thing you can do to survive a crash is to:

options.text: Wear a high-quality helmet that is securely fastened.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear a high-quality helmet that is securely fastened.
questions.explanation: Wearing a good helmet that fits properly and is fastened is the best way to increase your chances of surviving a crash.

questions.question: It is best to not ride directly alongside another vehicle because:

options.text: You may be riding in its blind spot.
It is distracting to have a vehicle next to you.
Other drivers may want to use the lane.
It would be difficult to see what is happening behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be riding in its blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding next to a vehicle is dangerous because the driver may not see you in their blind spot. The vehicle may also block your escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: To get the best protection, your helmet should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Meet Department of Transportation guidelines.
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards. It should fit snugly and have no visible damage.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should:

options.text: Try to squeeze into smaller gaps in traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride more slowly than usual.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight, which changes how your motorcycle handles. Your motorcycle will speed up more slowly, turn more slowly, and need more distance to stop. Ride more slowly, start slowing sooner, keep a larger space between you and other vehicles, and wait for bigger gaps in traffic.

questions.question: Most motorcycles:

options.text: Have brakes in both the front and rear.
Have three brakes: one in the front, one in the rear, and an emergency brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have brakes in both the front and rear.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have two brakes: one for the front wheel and one for the rear wheel.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, you should:

options.text: Prepare and adjust your motorcycle for the passenger.
Ride the same way as you would alone.
Make sure footrests are only for you.
Tell the passenger how to ride after you start.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prepare and adjust your motorcycle for the passenger.
questions.explanation: Your motorcycle must be properly equipped and adjusted to carry a passenger. Your motorcycle needs a separate footrest for the passenger and a large enough seat for two people. You may need to adjust your headlight, tire pressure, and suspension for the extra weight.

questions.question: ____ can remove alcohol from your body.
questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Only time can reduce alcohol in your body. Coffee, exercise, fresh air, and cold showers cannot lower your blood alcohol level or make you sober. They may help you stay awake, but they do not change your alcohol level.

questions.question: Which sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: Taking a turn too fast:

options.text: Is safe as long as you stay under the speed limit.
Is safer on a motorcycle than in a car.
Is safe as long as no other vehicles are nearby.
Can make you slide into another lane or off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can make you slide into another lane or off the road.
questions.explanation: Taking a turn too fast is dangerous. If you cannot control the turn, you may slide into another lane or leave the road. Always slow down before turning.

questions.question: What brakes do most motorcycles have?
questions.correctAnswerText: Front and rear
questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have one brake for each wheel. The front brake is stronger than the rear brake.

questions.question: Which of these does not need to be checked regularly?
questions.correctAnswerText: The paint
questions.explanation: Before each ride, check your tires, controls, chain, sprockets, shock absorbers, bolts, and brakes. A small problem on a motorcycle can be very dangerous.

questions.question: If you drink only one alcoholic drink:

options.text: Your judgment and riding ability can still be affected.
It usually has no effect on your body.
It affects your body but only for a short time.
It affects your body but coffee can remove it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your judgment and riding ability can still be affected.
questions.explanation: Even one drink can affect the skills you need to ride safely. Your body must have time to remove the alcohol. Drinking coffee does not help.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?
questions.correctAnswerText: Day and night
questions.explanation: Bright and reflective clothing helps others see you in all conditions. Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day, so wear bright clothing during daytime too.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?
questions.correctAnswerText: At night
questions.explanation: Wear reflective materials at night to make yourself more visible. Bright clothing with reflective materials helps other drivers see you.

questions.question: What is the main active ingredient in marijuana?
questions.correctAnswerText: THC
questions.explanation: THC (tetrahydrocannabinol) is the main active ingredient in marijuana.

questions.question: Long-term exposure to wind noise:

options.text: Is less damaging than listening to music.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can cause hearing loss.
questions.explanation: Long-term wind noise while riding can damage your hearing, even with a helmet. Wear proper hearing protection to prevent damage.

questions.question: Riding at night:

options.text: Is made safer by wearing reflective clothing.
Is not safe because other drivers cannot see your turn signals.
Should only be done in the city.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is made safer by wearing reflective clothing.
questions.explanation: Wear reflective materials when riding at night. This makes other drivers able to see you.

questions.question: When approaching an uneven surface, such as a bump or pothole, you should rise slightly off your seat:

options.text: So you can jump off the motorcycle if needed.
So your legs can absorb the shock.
So other drivers can see you better.
So you can get a better view of the uneven surface.

questions.correctAnswerText: So your legs can absorb the shock.
questions.explanation: Rising off your seat lets your legs and joints absorb the impact. This reduces the force felt by your body and helps keep you on the motorcycle.

questions.question: When riding, you should:

options.text: Always scan the road ahead and expect possible dangers.
Focus on the controls and speedometer instead of the road.
Not worry about hazards because there are very few on the road.
Always look ahead, but try not to look for hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always scan the road ahead and expect possible dangers.
questions.explanation: Look well ahead of your motorcycle to spot possible hazards early. This gives you more time to react safely.

questions.question: Do not ride directly next to another vehicle because:

options.text: Another driver may want to use your lane to pass.
You may be in the vehicle's blind spot.
You may have access to escape routes.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding beside another vehicle is dangerous. You may be in their blind spot and the driver will not see you. The vehicle may also block your escape route if a hazard appears.
